summary: This is Snowflake documentation for the CREATE SECURITY INTEGRATION (SAML2) SQL command, which creates or replaces a SAML2 security integration providing single sign-on between Snowflake and a third-party Identity Provider. It gives the syntax, required parameters (name, TYPE, ENABLED, SAML2_ISSUER, SAML2_SSO_URL, SAML2_PROVIDER, SAML2_X509_CERT), the many optional parameters, access control requirements (CREATE INTEGRATION privilege, ACCOUNTADMIN by default), usage notes on atomic CREATE OR REPLACE, and an AD FS example.
one_line: Snowflake SQL reference for creating or replacing a SAML2 single sign-on security integration with a third-party identity provider.
key_facts: CREATE SECURITY INTEGRATION (SAML2) creates a new SAML2 security integration in the account or replaces an existing integration.
A SAML2 security integration provides single sign-on (SSO) workflows by creating an interface between Snowflake and a third-party Identity Provider (IdP).
Required parameters include name, TYPE = SAML2, ENABLED, SAML2_ISSUER, SAML2_SSO_URL, SAML2_PROVIDER, and SAML2_X509_CERT.
SAML2_PROVIDER must be one of the following: OKTA, ADFS, Custom.
SAML2_X509_CERT is the Base64 encoded IdP signing certificate on a single line without the BEGIN CERTIFICATE and END CERTIFICATE markers.
ALLOWED_USER_DOMAINS is a list of email domains that can authenticate with a SAML2 security integration.
ALLOWED_EMAIL_PATTERNS is a list of regular expressions that email addresses are matched against to authenticate with a SAML2 security integration.
If SAML2_REQUESTED_NAMEID_FORMAT is not specified, Snowflake sends the urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress value in the authentication request to the IdP.
SAML2_FORCE_AUTHN defaults to FALSE; when TRUE, Snowflake sets the ForceAuthn SAML parameter to TRUE in the outgoing request to the identity provider.
SAML2_POST_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URL is the endpoint to which Snowflake redirects users after clicking the Log Out button in the Classic Console.
The CREATE INTEGRATION privilege on the account is required and only the ACCOUNTADMIN role has it by default.
CREATE OR REPLACE statements are atomic: the old object is deleted and the new object is created in a single transaction.
The example creates an Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) integration named my_idp with SAML2_SP_INITIATED_LOGIN_PAGE_LABEL = 'my_idp' and SAML2_ENABLE_SP_INITIATED = false.
Customers should not enter personal data (other than for a User object), sensitive data, export-controlled data, or other regulated data as metadata.
